summary.en: A loop repeats one controlled statement.
summary.bn: একই কাজ বারবার করতে loop বেছে নাও এবং শুরুতে ও শেষে শর্ত দেখার পার্থক্য বোঝো।

notes: All three loop forms exist in C89. C99 permits a variable declaration inside a for header. The C17 examples use that convenient form and consistently brace the loop bodies.

examples.title: Repeat a counted action
examples.explanationHtml: The counter begins at one and reaches three inside the body. Increment then makes it four, so the next condition fails. Three labeled lines appear, each produced by the same source statement with a different counter value.

examples.title: Skip a pre-test body
examples.explanationHtml: The starting condition is false because no seats remain. The body never runs, and Done is printed afterward. This zero-iteration behavior is often exactly what an empty workload requires.

examples.title: Compare a post-test body
examples.explanationHtml: The body prints Menu before checking remaining. The false condition then stops repetition. Compared with the previous example, moving the test changes whether the initial body runs, even though the starting value is identical.

practice.title: Count roll lines
practice.statementHtml: Read n 0 to 10. After the prompt Input: , print Roll i for i from 1 to n, each on a separate line. For zero, print no roll lines.
hints: The false initial test handles zero work.

practice.title: Count down seats
practice.statementHtml: Read n 0 to 10. After the prompt Input: , print each positive remaining count from n down to 1, one per line.
hints: Update the value used by the condition.

practice.title: At least one announcement
practice.statementHtml: Read n 0 to 5. After the prompt Input: , print Menu once for n=0; otherwise n times, each with newline.
hints: The post-test loop provides the first action.

practice.title: Sum a counted workload
practice.statementHtml: Read n 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print the sum of 1 through n and newline.
hints: The empty sum starts at zero.

quiz.prompt: Which loops check before their body?
quiz.explanation: Both pre-test forms may run zero iterations.

quiz.prompt: Which loop naturally guarantees an initial menu display?
quiz.explanation: Its body comes before its repeat test.
The body is the work repeated under the loop rule.

options: A special input value signaling stop
quiz.explanation: It is excluded from ordinary data processing.

quiz.prompt: Which loop is usually clearest for a simple known count?
quiz.explanation: Its header collects the counter progression.

quiz.prompt: What should a loop trace include after the last body?
options: The final condition that stops repetition
quiz.explanation: The failed test explains why the body does not run again.

quiz.prompt: What often causes accidental infinite repetition?
options: A missing update or missing input progress
quiz.explanation: The state never moves toward a false condition.

quiz.prompt: A for starts at one and stops before four. How many stars appear?
quiz.explanation: The body runs for one, two and three.

quiz.prompt: A while begins with zero remaining. Which message survives?
quiz.explanation: The initial test skips the body.

quiz.prompt: A do-while has a false repeat test. How many body messages appear?
quiz.explanation: The body precedes the first test.

keyPoints.en: A loop repeats one controlled statement.
keyPoints.bn: loop একটি statement বা block বারবার চালায়।

keyPoints.en: While and for check before their body.
keyPoints.bn: while আর for আগে শর্ত দেখে।

keyPoints.en: Do-while normally runs its body at least once.
keyPoints.bn: do-while-এ সাধারণভাবে body অন্তত একবার চলে।

keyPoints.en: A sentinel signals the end of input data.
keyPoints.bn: sentinel মানে ইনপুটের data শেষ করার সংকেত।

keyPoints.en: A terminating loop needs progress toward exit.
keyPoints.bn: থামার জন্য loop-কে exit-এর দিকে এগোতে হয়।

examQuestions.question: Which loops check before their body?
examQuestions.answerHtml: while and for. Both pre-test forms may run zero iterations.

examQuestions.question: Which loop naturally guarantees an initial menu display?
examQuestions.answerHtml: do-while. Its body comes before its repeat test.

***

The body runs for one, two and three.

examQuestions.question: Read n 0 to 100. After Input: print the sum of 1 through n and newline.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int n;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 0 || n > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    int sum = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        sum += i;
    }
    printf("%d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}

The empty sum starts at zero.
